exits.notes: The 8-K and the 2020 proxy say only that he 'left the Company' (no reason given), so exit_type is 'other'. No filing reports any separation payment: his FY2019 SCT row shows All Other Compensation of $1,600 (ride credits) and he is not in the 2020 Potential Payments table, which covers only NEOs employed at 2019-12-31. His amended employment agreement gave 12 months of extra time-based vesting if he was 'involuntarily terminated' in his first 24 months (he joined March 2018). No filing says whether that applied. All components are null because none is quantified.

exits.role: Executive Vice President and Chief Product Officer
exits.notes: His officer role ended in March 2020 (8-K: he 'will no longer serve' as EVP and CPO). He stayed on as EVP, Strategic Initiatives (not an officer) and 'left the Company in December 2020' (no day or reason given; exit_date is month precision). In the 2021 proxy's Potential Payments table, his row (qualifying termination not in connection with a change of control) shows dashes for base salary, COBRA, accelerated equity and total. Because he had already left, that row is read as the actual amount: nothing. His FY2020 SCT All Other Compensation ($1,106) has no severance item. Consulting is null because no advisory arrangement is disclosed.

exits.role: Executive Vice President, Rideshare and Engineering
exits.notes: He 'will step down' as EVP, Rideshare and Engineering (8-K 2021-03-22) and stopped being an executive officer in March 2021. His employment was expected to 'terminate' on 2021-05-31, when he would get Executive Severance Plan severance and COBRA. No filing states the reason beyond 'step down', so exit_type is 'other'. The amounts come from the 2021 proxy's Potential Payments row, which the proxy says is 'the amount expected to be provided to him upon his expected employment termination date on May 31, 2021': $225,000 base salary (6 months) and $11,843 COBRA (recorded as other_exit_pay), with a dash for accelerated equity. The filing states the total of $236,843. As an advisor to 2021-11-20 he got 'no compensation other than continued vesting', so consulting_fees is 0. The value of that continued vesting is not quantified (accelerated_equity_value is null). He was not an NEO in later proxies, so no filing confirms the actual payment or date.

He 'resigned as an employee effective December 1, 2021' and so forfeited Executive Severance Plan benefits. Under a separation agreement he got a $75,000 cash payment for a release of claims. Under a consulting agreement to 2022-06-01, his consideration was continued vesting of 73,793 RSUs (14,627 + 40,686 + 18,480 shares). No market value of those shares is stated; the ASC 718 modification figures in the proxy are a net $491,025 benefit to the company, which is not a value received. So accelerated_equity_value is null. 'Accelerated vesting was not provided.' No cash consulting fee is described, so consulting_fees is null. His vested options' post-termination exercise period was extended to the original term (not valued). The FY2021 SCT All Other of $1,941 is final-paycheck wages and life insurance, not exit pay. total_exit_pay is null because the continued vesting is not valued.

He 'has decided to transition from his role as CEO' (8-K 2023-03-27). He became non-employee Board Chair and a one-year non-employee advisor, so exit_type is 'other'. Severance is 0: he is 'not entitled to severance benefits under the Executive Severance Plan'. consulting_fees of $450,000 is the Advisory Cash Fee in his Transition Agreement (equal to his final base salary, paid over 12 months). The agreement also pays 12 months of COBRA premiums, but no filing gives a full-period amount, so other_exit_pay is null. Payments actually reported: FY2023 SCT 'advisory and COBRA fees' of $319,653, and in the FY2024 director table $112,500 of consulting fees plus $7,370 of COBRA. Those add up to less than $450,000 (see conflicts). His equity kept vesting while he stayed a service provider (not valued). Time-based awards would accelerate only if his board service ended other than by voluntary resignation. He resigned from the board on 2025-08-14, so no acceleration is reported. The $260,005 RSU granted under the agreement at the 2023 annual meeting is treated as director pay (it is in the FY2023 director table), not exit pay. The FY2023 SCT also lists $15,000 of attorney fees, which the filing does not tie to the transition. total_exit_pay is null because the COBRA total and the continued vesting are not quantified.

The 8-K says the company and Ms. Paul 'mutually agreed to terms pursuant to which she would step down as CFO'. The 2024 proxy calls it her 'resignation of employment' (see conflicts). The 8-K says the departure was not the result of any dispute or disagreement. She got $325,000 cash (six months' salary) plus a lump sum for six months of COBRA. The 2024 Potential Payments row, which the proxy says shows the actual payments, gives COBRA as $15,966, a dash for accelerated equity, and a total of $340,966. The SCT footnote calls the $340,966 'severance'. She was an advisor to 2023-11-30, paid only in continued vesting: no advisory fee appears in her FY2023 SCT All Other, so consulting_fees is 0. The value of that continued vesting is not quantified (null); awards vesting after 2023-11-30 were forfeited. Her FY2023 relocation services ($77,697) and tax gross-ups ($40,729) continue a 2022 relocation benefit and are not described as exit pay, so they are excluded. total_exit_pay is the filing-stated $340,966, which equals the recorded components.

exits.role: Executive Vice President, Head of Rideshare
exits.notes: The 2023-03-27 8-K says that, as part of the CEO transition, the rideshare organization would report directly to the CEO and he 'will step down' as EVP, Head of Rideshare on 2023-05-22. The 2024 proxy describes his 'resignation of employment', so exit_type is 'resigned'. His terms were first set in a 2023-03-27 memorandum of understanding. He got $325,000 cash (about six months' salary) and $15,966 for six months of COBRA (actual per the 2024 Potential Payments row), with a dash for accelerated equity and a total of $340,966. The SCT footnote calls the $340,966 'severance'. He was an advisor to 2023-11-30, paid only in continued vesting: no advisory fee appears in his FY2023 SCT, so consulting_fees is 0. The value of that continued vesting is not quantified (null); awards vesting after 2023-11-30 were forfeited. total_exit_pay is the filing-stated $340,966, which equals the recorded components.

He 'has decided to transition from his role as President' (8-K 2023-03-27). He stayed Vice Chair as a non-employee director and became a one-year non-employee advisor, so exit_type is 'other'. Severance is 0: he is 'not entitled to severance benefits under the Executive Severance Plan'. consulting_fees of $450,000 is the advisory cash payment in his Transition Agreement (equal to his final base salary). The agreement also pays 12 months of COBRA premiums, but no full-period amount is stated, so other_exit_pay is null. Payments actually reported: FY2023 SCT 'advisory and COBRA fees' of $240,966, and in the FY2024 director table $187,500 of consulting fees plus $13,305 of COBRA. Those add up to less than $450,000 (see conflicts). His equity kept vesting while he stayed a service provider (not valued). He resigned from the board on 2025-08-14, so the agreement's acceleration on a non-voluntary end of board service did not apply. The $260,005 RSU granted under the agreement is treated as director pay. The FY2023 SCT also lists $15,000 of attorney fees and $704,388 of personal security, which the filing does not tie to the transition. total_exit_pay is null.

The 8-K says she 'and the Company agreed to terms pursuant to which Ms. Sverchek will depart the Company as an employee'. It also says 'the circumstances of Ms. Sverchek's departure' qualified her for Executive Severance Plan benefits and that the departure was not the result of any dispute or disagreement. Severance cash is $1,137,500 = $650,000 (12 months' salary, enhanced under her 2023 President letter agreement) + $487,500 (prorated 2024 bonus). The SCT footnote states the $1,137,500 total. Her President letter-agreement RSUs vested in full: $2,368,992 at the $11.29 close on 2024-08-20, per the 2025 Potential Payments row, which the proxy says shows the actual payments. The SCT instead shows a $437,048 ASC 718 charge, which it says 'is not reflective of the actual amount received'. Advisory fees of $34,071 (a $10,000 monthly retainer to 2024-11-30) appear in the FY2024 SCT. Her other equity kept vesting during the advisory period (not valued), and awards vesting after 2024-11-30 were forfeited. other_exit_pay is the $33,462 COBRA lump sum. total_exit_pay is null: the filing's stated total of $3,539,954 (salary + bonus + COBRA + equity) leaves out the $34,071 advisory fees, and the plain sum of the recorded components ($3,574,025) is not stated in any filing.

The 8-K says only that she 'will depart the Company effective March 6, 2025' and that the departure 'is not the result of any dispute or disagreement'. No reason is given, so exit_type is 'other'. She was an NEO only for FY2023, as interim CFO. No filing discloses what she actually received: she was not an NEO in the 2025 or 2026 proxies, and no separation agreement was filed. The 2024 proxy's Potential Payments table is the only quantification. It is hypothetical, as of 2023-12-31, for a qualifying termination not in connection with a change of control: $200,000 base salary (six months), $15,966 COBRA, a dash for accelerated equity, total $215,966. Those figures are recorded as an estimate. They apply only if her 2025 departure was a qualifying (involuntary or good-reason) termination, which the filings do not say.

She 'will retire from her position as CFO' effective 2026-09-28 (8-K 2026-09-09), and the departure 'is not the result of any dispute or disagreement'. She serves as an advisor from 2026-09-28 to 2026-12-15. The only consideration disclosed is continued vesting of her outstanding equity during that term (not valued); no cash consulting fee is described. The 8-K mentions no severance or other cash. All components are null until the 2027 proxy (FY2026 SCT) reports what was paid.

conflicts.description: Founders' advisory fees. The 8-K, Green's Transition Agreement (Exhibit 10.2) and the 2024 proxy say each founder would receive $450,000 of advisory cash over 12 months, plus 12 months of COBRA premiums. The amounts reported as paid are lower. Green: FY2023 SCT 'advisory and COBRA fees' $319,653, plus FY2024 director table $112,500 consulting and $7,370 COBRA, for $439,523 in all. Zimmer: $240,966, plus $187,500 and $13,305, for $441,771 in all. Even before COBRA is taken out, each total is below $450,000. No filing explains the gap (for example, an installment paid outside the two years). The exit rows record the $450,000 agreement amount.

Elaine Paul's exit type. The 2023-05-16 8-K says the company and Ms. Paul 'mutually agreed to terms pursuant to which she would step down as CFO'. The 2024 proxy describes Paul's and Raj's 'resignation of employment'. Recorded as 'mutual', the 8-K's more specific wording. Raj, for whom no mutual-agreement wording appears, is recorded as 'resigned'.

Double reporting in FY2023. Green's ($63,544 fees, $260,005 RSU) and Zimmer's ($20,110 fees, $260,005 RSU) non-employee director pay appears both in the FY2023 Director Compensation table and in their FY2023 Summary Compensation Table rows (salary includes the director fees; stock awards include the RSU). Risher's pre-CEO director fees appear in the director table ($13,046 including RSUs in lieu worth $11,178). The SCT says his salary 'includes $1,868 in director fees received in the form of 1,136 RSUs with a total grant date fair value of $11,178': the share count matches the director table, but the dollar figure does not, and $13,046 - $11,178 = $1,868. Director rows are recorded as printed; anyone adding them to the exec comp file should take out the overlap.

How RSUs taken in lieu of cash are reported changed. In the FY2022 table (2023 proxy), directors who took RSUs instead of cash (Lawee, Cohen, Risher) show lower cash fees and Stock Awards above the $260,000 annual award ($275,001, $272,126 and $271,247). From the FY2023 table on, such RSUs are 'reported as though they had been paid in cash' in the fees column. Rows are recorded as printed, so the cash/stock split is not comparable across these years; totals are.

open_questions: Erin Brewer retired as CFO on 2026-09-28. Whether she gets anything beyond continued vesting during her advisory term (to 2026-12-15) will first appear in the 2027 proxy (FY2026 SCT).

Lisa Blackwood-Kapral (left 2025-03-06): no filing says whether her departure was a qualifying termination or what she was paid. Her exit row uses the 2023 year-end hypothetical (basis 'estimated'). The Q1 2025 10-Q filed no separation agreement.
Jon McNeill (left 2019-07-29): his agreement gave 12 months of extra vesting on an involuntary termination in his first 24 months. No filing says whether it was triggered, or whether he got any cash.
Eisar Lipkovitz: the 2021 proxy gives the expected severance ($236,843) and termination date (2021-05-31). No later filing confirms either, because he was not an NEO in the 2022 proxy.

The founders' 2025 annual director RSUs ($260,003 each, granted 2025-06-05): Green and Zimmer resigned from the board on 2025-08-14, before the first quarterly vest date, and are absent from the 2025 year-end outstanding-awards table. No filing says the awards were forfeited. Their Transition Agreements accelerate time-based awards only when board service ends other than by voluntary resignation.

Mikitani's 2020 annual award ($260,001, granted 2020-06-19, resigned 2020-08-31) and Miura-Ko's forfeited 2019 award are recorded at grant-date value as printed. Neither table shows the value realized.

The IPO prospectus (424B4, 2019-03-29) has a FY2018 non-employee director table (only Jarrett $225,389 and Wilderotter $450,778 got stock awards; everyone else shows dashes). It is not a proxy, so it is not recorded here.

coverage.method: Director Compensation table rows from every Lyft proxy filed 2019-2026: DEF 14A 2020-04-27 (FY2019), 2021-04-28 (FY2020), 2022-04-29 (FY2021), 2023-05-01 (FY2022), 2024-04-25 (FY2023), the 2025 DEFC14A 0001759509-25-000069 filed 2025-04-24 (FY2024; that year's annual proxy was a contested solicitation), and DEF 14A 2026-04-10 (FY2025). That is one row per (filing, director), 59 rows. No proxy was filed in 2019 (IPO 2019-03-29; first annual meeting 2020). Checked and found to have no director table: the 2022 10-K/A (Part III incorporated by reference to the 2022 proxy), the 2025 DEFR14A (board-change supplement), and Engine Capital's DEFC14A (0000921895-25-001184). Every row's components sum exactly to its printed total. No Lyft director table has option, non-equity incentive or pension/NQDC columns.

One exit row for each of the 11 NEOs in lyft_exec_comp_research.json whose employment or officer tenure ended through 2026-10-02 (title changes and interim roles are not exits): McNeill, Makavy, Lipkovitz, Roberts, Green, Paul, Raj, Zimmer, Sverchek, Blackwood-Kapral and Brewer. Sources: the proxy after each departure (CD&A transition and separation sections, SCT All Other Compensation footnotes, Potential Payments tables, which Lyft uses to report actual severance for departed NEOs), every 8-K Item 5.02 in the EDGAR submissions feed through 2026-10-02, the Green Transition Agreement (8-K Exhibit 10.2), and the exhibit lists of the 10-Qs following each departure. Advisory-period continued vesting is never valued in the filings, so accelerated_equity_value is null except for Sverchek's contractual full vesting.
